pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

12. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Glucose and oxygen

2. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

4. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. B — Producers

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

8. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

10. D — Ice melting to water

11. C — newton (N)

12. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water hardness; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reproduction in plants; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of The Interdependence of Life; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
